newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BORSODCHEM RALLIES ON TAX RELIEF NEWS.
newsitem.headline: BORSODCHEM RALLIES ON TAX RELIEF NEWS.

text.p: Hungarian chemicals company Borsodchem shares rallied in early trading on the Budapest bourse on Wednesday on tax relief news, traders said.
Borsodchem's chief executive officer confirmed to Reuters that they expected 50 or 100 percent tax relief for 1997, stemming from Hungary's tax regulations
"We expect a tax relief of 50 or 100 percent," Borsodchem's CEO Laszlo F. Kovacs told Reuters, adding that this was no special favour to the company.
Borsodchem shares opened at 4,720 forints, just above Tuesday's close of 4,715 forints and rapidly rose to a new record high of 5,120 forints.

Kovacs added that a company is entitled to 50 percent tax relief if it increased exports by at least 25 percent or 600 million forints in 1997 over 1996 or had a productive investment of at least one billion forints last year. Borsodchem meets both requirements, he said.
"We will certainly increase our export that much...and last year invested over one billion forints in our MDI plant," Kovacs said.
At 1141 GMT Borsodchem shares stood at 5,140 forints, up 425.
